Owono had raced out of his goal and crashed into De Miguel in added time at the end of the Spanish second division match on Monday afternoon, causing the striker to experience a cardiorespiratory arrest. quietus.title: Open Mind, Open Planet: Gigi Masin’s Favourite Albums
quietus.description: As his cult classic 1986 album Wind receives an expanded reissue, Italian composer and ambient pioneer Gigi Masin takes Siobhan Kane through his life in 13 records The renewed interest in Gigi Masin’s 1986 album Wind has taken the Venetian by surprise. He sees it as “strange and wonderful… I am really happy and honoured”. The expanded album, reissued by Numero Uno 40 years later, recontextualises Wind as an ambient gem, but an appreciation for Masin started some time ago, with artists such as Björk referencing his work, sampling ‘Clouds’ on her 2002 song ‘It’s In Our Hands’. Growing up in Italy, playing the guitar and working in radio, Masin was exposed to lots of different kinds of music,…

quietus.title: A Dream Within a Dream: Manifold of Partially Actualized Realities by Randall Dunn
quietus.description: The American composer, producer and audio engineer warps time and space on a slow-burning album that riffs on Philip K. Dick's "orthogonal" temporalities Photo credit Charmaine Lee Imagine your entire life, your entire world, being dreamed into existence by a creator who, night after night, gradually gives shape to your being, only to discover that he, too, is someone else’s dream. This is the premise of Jorge Luis Borges’ short story ‘The Circular Ruins’, after which Randall Dunn christened his Brooklyn studio. He’s the man behind the production of some of the highest peaks in experimental metal, from Earth’s The Bees Made Honey in the Lion’s Skull to Sunn O)))’s monumental Monoliths &…

It would indeed be fun, were it not for the call bell that keeps cutting in, turning fun into fun-ding – a never-ending, soul-sucking loop. Silence falls after ‘decision pen-ding’. This semantic, even conceptual playfulness of ‘Ding’ permeates Vanity Project, which gathers pieces from 2008 to 2026. Ingamells is the sole musician on all but one track, speaking, singing, playing melodica,…

quietus.title: Funny Games: Aphex Twin’s Richard D. James Album 30 years on
quietus.description: With a manic grin leering from the cover, Aphex Twin's fourth was readily incorporated into blather about drill & bass but his best, most cohesive album was neither wacky nor a novelty, says Toby Manning Richard D. James Album by Aphex Twin The year is 1996, the era of Britpop and lads’ mags, of Euro 96 and ‘Three Lions’, the retro complacency of which has seemingly no connection to the restlessly innovative Aphex Twin’s fifth album. Yet the depthless positivity of Cool Britannia didn’t just produce Britpop but ‘comedy is the new rock & roll’, the wipe-clean irony of Chris Evans and the music weeklies’ suffusion with puns, gags and exclamations of ‘arse!’ This comedification of culture…

aquariumdrunkard.description: Soundsystem check. A lost star of early ’80s dancehall, Billy Boyo was just fourteen when he recorded Zim Zim in London in 1983. One of the era’s great young singjays, Boyo moves between vocal and dub across twelve tracks, his delivery drifting over heavyweight riddims before disappearing into the mix. Full of swagger yet mellow and unhurried, he rides the bass-heavy arrangements through a thick haze of echo and reverb.

aquariumdrunkard.description: Welcome back to Aquarium Drunkard Transmissions with your host Jason P. Woodbury. We've entered the holidays, aka the official "Vince Guaraldi Season." This week on the show, we're digging into the work of Guaraldi with Peanuts historian and author of Vince Guaraldi at the Piano, Derrick Bang. We discuss it all: Guaraldi's fascination with the bossa nova sound in the late '50s, his status as a composer who didn't write or read music—writing from a purely melodic standpoint, his work with Brazilian guitarist Bola Sete; his groundbreaking Grace Cathedral Jazz Mass; and of course, his work on the animated Peanuts specials. Plus, we explore that lingering mystery: did Vince Guaraldi ever play…

aquariumdrunkard.description: La Ola Nocturna is the third installment of Bongo Joe’s highly successful series on experimental pop in post-Franco Spain, and the first to chart the wave after dark. If La Contra Ola crowned the industrial liturgies of Esplendor Geométrico and the electronic punk of Aviador Dro, and La Ola Interior drifted through the ambient, exotica, and proto-Balearic landscapes of Miguel A. Ruiz and post-minimalists like Javier Segura and Finis Africae, who carried the Fourth World Music of Jon Hassell and Brian Eno into Iberia, this new volume walks the borderlands between those territories, where left-field pop grew in parallel to unorthodox experiments, and in Madrid, but also in the smaller indie…

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Clientele :: Suburban Light
aquariumdrunkard.description: It can be difficult to verbalize exactly what autumnal records are capable of eliciting. One thing is undeniable: October and November are the months for The Clientele's 2000 debut album Suburban Light . Perhaps most impressive, the uninitiated would never detect that such an accomplished record was comprised mostly of a smattering of the band's earlier 7" singles from the years prior. Though ideal for any season, the record is an impeccable collection of reveries that paint a viscerally evocative picture of sundown strolls with scattered leaves underfoot.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Steve Gunn :: Sundowner
aquariumdrunkard.description: A long neglected album dates to the beginning of Steve Gunn’s career, when it seemed that the guitarist might become a Takoma-style picker rather than the songwriter/improvisational experimenter he has since turned out to be. The playing is agile and folk-blues focused; the singing, when it comes, is similarly traditional and not as polished as Gunn has become. The music earned the approval of no less than Jack Rose, and its reels and rambles and psychedelic drones feel very much of a piece with the master’s work.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Chrome Chasm :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: The Houston-based trio known as Chrome Chasm features three veteran improvisers doing what they do best — improvising. Together, guitarist Tom Carter (Charalambides), saxophonist/flautist Mlee Marie (Hearts of Animals) and pedal steel-er Will Adams (Lower Dens, Ka-Nives) create bewitching, twilit music that’s somehow both minimalist and wide-open — a vast landscape that somehow contains countless sonic details. Aquarium Drunkard chatted with Tom, Mlee and Will to find out more.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Miles Davis: Europe ‘71
aquariumdrunkard.description: Across the Miles Davis electric era there’s no greater divide than that between 1972’s On the Corner and what came before it. But the signposts are there if you know where to look, with recordings from a European tour in the fall of ‘71 revealing Miles subtly, deftly moving the pieces into place for his next iteration.

mubi.title: Can This Be Dixie?: Building the Hollywood South
mubi.description: Hallelujah (King Vidor, 1929). The American South exists only in the imagination, yet it’s as real as sin. It cannot merely be the land situated beneath the Mason-Dixon (the historical survey line that traditionally demarcated Northern and Southern states), whose citizens fought under the banner of the Confederacy; one cannot ignore the obviously Southern states of West Virginia and Kentucky, or the political split between West and East Tennessee. It cannot be a shared culture or a shared history, for the residents of Jacksonville, Florida, find little in common with those families tucked deep in the Appalachian hollers or those ruling the oil-rich cities of eastern Texas. At the 51st Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), which saw the inaugural edition of its official content market, the atmosphere was unmistakably different from its jubilee year. The spirit of nostalgic celebration and victory lapping from 2025's "TIFFty" celebration had evaporated, leaving behind the gritty residue of cinema as a commercial product. Lacking the elegance of “Marché du Film” at Cannes and the specificity of “European Film Market” at Berlinale, for their new industry initiative TIFF settled on a name that evokes the absurdity of local hero Matt Johnson’s Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie (2025). In her memoir, Varda par Agnès , the French director describes herself as “une féministe de terrain plus qu’une discuteuse,” roughly translated as “a feminist on the ground rather than in theory.” Later in the book, she describes the “feminists” discussing her work, implying that she was outside this group. How feminist she reads from any angle now is unclear. Many would, for instance, find her focus on the body and childbirth essentialist. Her 1975 short, Réponse de femmes: Notre corps, notre sexe ( Women Reply: Our Bodies, Our Sex ), opens with this prompt: “What does it mean to be a woman?” The text is painted on glass and held up by two…

nplusone.title: Trump’s Microphones
nplusone.description: Trump is alone, photographed from below (presumably by a crouching photographer, though I never see one on the ground) so as to appear more monumental. More often than not, his arms are half-raised at his sides and his palms are up, like he’s fending off the press, rhetorically, with his habitual “Who, me?” gesture. He is encircled by a panoply of black shapes jutting in, which evokes cartoon compositions where the main character is overwhelmingly surrounded, by knives, or the Feds, or meddling kids.

nplusone.title: EV Listening
nplusone.description: The Honda Prologue has a hovering, suffusing melody, with a low rhythmic pulse and a subtle, epiphanic wash. It sounds like a computer game lifting you into heaven, or the arrival of benevolent extraterrestrial colonists. The Porsche Taycan makes a more sinister and comic, gulping, warp-speed sound, and the Nissan Ariya gives off a disturbed digital whine, like the tantrums of a petulant robot.
